title: Responsibility over Plants
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner describes the responsibilities God gave people over plants (Genesis 1:29; 2:15: food, care, cultivation), applies them to conservation (planting trees, not burning), and discusses how responsible use of plants grows the economy (cash crops, timber, fruit, jobs).

floor.prerequisite: Knows people were given work in the garden.
floor.question: What does Genesis 2:15 ask people to do?
floor.answer: Work the garden and take care of it

steps: Name cash crops in the area.

board.do: Draw a tree and its uses around it.

board.say: What happens if we cut without planting?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say the trees run out, soil erodes.

misconceptions.ask: A family cuts trees for charcoal every month. What does stewardship ask?
misconceptions.repair: Show the cost: a tree takes years to grow. Plan a "cut one, plant two" rule for the school.

listen_for: Only to make the earth beautiful
misconceptions.ask: Why did God give plants, according to Genesis 1:29?
misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 1:29 and 2:9: plants for food and beauty.

listen_for: It cannot; plants are only food
misconceptions.ask: How can responsible use of plants help the economy?
misconceptions.repair: Name crops grown for sale in the area and what the money pays for.

listen_for: Yes, it is the quickest way
misconceptions.ask: A farmer burns the bush to clear land every year. Is this responsible use of plants?
misconceptions.repair: List effects of burning on soil and wildlife; compare with clearing and composting.

checks.question: Why did God give plants, according to Genesis 1:29?
How can plants help the economy?
checks.answer: Cash crops and timber bring income and jobs
